- Billable utilization is inaccurate without Cognition 360.
- UX is antiquated, driving DeskDirector adoption.
- Project management is slow and difficult.
- Customer portal/report sharing is limited.
- Invoice customization is expensive and slow.
- ConnectWise CRM is not usable, requiring Salesforce.

**Mitigation:** Demo sales orders, inventory, purchasing, receiving, mobile, projects, and physical security/AV workflows.

**Risk:** Multiple stakeholders may have different priorities.  

**Mitigation:** Tailor recap and demo agenda by department, then map follow-up breakouts to finance, service delivery, operations, and executive needs.

current.Business_Issue_Details__c: Prime Secured operates two distinct service lines—security integration (about 85% of revenue) and managed IT—across ConnectWise and Autotask. This split creates fragmented customer records, manual ticket handoffs, and limited visibility across shared accounts. Its project accounting also resembles construction: long-running projects require work-in-progress tracking, percentage-of-completion revenue recognition, phased billing, and AIA-style payment schedules. Neither current PSA supports these requirements natively, forcing spreadsheet workarounds and additional administrative effort.
current.Business_Issues__c: Single Points of Failure across employee resources
current.Problems__c:
- WIP and revenue recognition are calculated manually in spreadsheets, including projects spanning multiple years.
- ConnectWise lacks the project financial oversight and margin visibility Prime Secured needs.
- AIA payment schedules and forms are not handled natively by the current systems.
- Joint security/MSP customers require manual Teams-based routing between ConnectWise and Autotask, creating risk of missed requests.
- Two PSAs increase operating complexity, duplicate processes, and contribute to extra headcount.
- A future migration must account for an expected ConnectWise renewal around January.
current.Values__c: Rev.io can consolidate operational and financial workflows around a billing-first PSA. The strongest value is native project percentage invoicing, deposits, phase-level billing, remaining-balance tracking, and margin visibility—reducing spreadsheet dependence and improving financial control. A unified platform can also remove manual handoffs between the security and managed IT teams, lower administrative burden, and create one customer and service history. Additional value comes from Revy AI reporting, Teams-assisted ticket workflows, dispatch/GPS, inventory and asset tracking, native quoting/e-signature, flexible multi-DBA configuration, and month-to-month seat-based pricing without module add-ons
current.Risk_Mitigation_Plan__c:
- **Product-fit risk:** AIA forms and construction-style revenue recognition may require workflow validation. **Mitigation:** Be precise about native capabilities versus configured processes; use realistic project examples in the demo.
- **Migration risk:** Replacing two PSAs at once would be disruptive. **Mitigation:** Recommend a phased migration with clear data, integration, and cutover milestones.
- **Timing risk:** A January ConnectWise renewal may compress the evaluation. **Mitigation:** Confirm the exact date immediately and work backward from the renewal.
- **Change-management risk:** Teams are accustomed to separate systems and manual handoffs. **Mitigation:** Map shared-client workflows and quantify avoided touches, missed tickets, and administrative hours.
- **Decision risk:** Economic buyer and formal success criteria are not yet known. **Mitigation:** Identify both during the demo and agree on measurable validation criteria

current.Business_Issue_Details__c: Slice Wireless Solutions (about 10 staff, New York) runs Autotask for CRM, quoting and service, with QuickBooks Desktop and spreadsheets on the side. Autotask never integrated with QuickBooks, so installs and upgrades get relayed to billing by message and sometimes go unbilled. Quotes take about 30 minutes, and techs fill in tickets after the fact. John Hutzler says there is consensus to replace Autotask, but no date or trigger yet.
current.Business_Issues__c: Broken Relationship with a Rev.io Competitor
current.Problems__c:
- Quoting in Autotask takes about 30 minutes for a simple quote; John's spreadsheet takes 5
- Autotask never integrated with QuickBooks Desktop, so billing is manual; "the big issue really is QuickBooks"
- Service upgrades (50 to 100 meg, $50 to $100 more a month) don't flow back to billing, "a few times a quarter"
- Past installs went unbilled for a month before the process was cleaned up
- Techs don't use Autotask in the field and fill in tickets afterward; CFO wants install time tracked
- Contract renewal reminders in Autotask are "not very good"
- Autotask project management tried on larger projects and "never worked"
- Leads live in a separate pre-sales CRM, customers in Autotask, estimates in a spreadsheet
- Wants install details pinned at the top of each client record
current.Solutions__c:
- One customer record holds the lead, quote, project, ticket, agreement and invoice, so a signed quote becomes the order and the invoice without retyping
- Quotes show cost, margin and tax and support product bundles for faster Wi-Fi gear quotes
- Recurring services and agreements drive billing, so a service upgrade (50 to 100 meg) is picked up from the work instead of relayed to the office
- Mobile app gives techs timers, parts, photos and signature capture, so install time reaches the invoice and the CFO gets profitability
- Projects carry phases and budgeted hours for larger installs
current.Values__c:
Quote time moves from about 30 minutes toward the 5 minutes John gets from his spreadsheet.

- Billing leakage stops: each missed upgrade costs $50 to $100 a month until someone catches it, and it happens a few times a quarter. 

-Re-keying between Autotask, QuickBooks and spreadsheets goes away, and tech time on installs finally feeds an invoice and a profitability view for the CFO. Moving pre-sales into Rev.io removes one system. Current Autotask spend is an estimate near $850 a month (10 users at about $85, unverified).
- hours a week on quoting and billing, unbilled dollars to date.
current.Risk_Mitigation_Plan__c:
Risk: No compelling event; Autotask term unclear (John says he thinks month-to-month) 

Risk: Economic buyer not identified and John is the only contact. Mitigation: ask John to bring "my boss" and the CFO to the demo.

Risk: QuickBooks Desktop integration claim, after Autotask's promise never worked. Mitigation: verify connector status with Tony and show the sync, not a statement.
Risk: Competition and do-nothing not explored; earlier attempts to switch "in fits and starts" stalled. Mitigation: ask what stopped them before and who else they are considering.

Risk: Pricing on a 10-person team. Mitigation: get the seat mix first and confirm pricing before quoting a number.

previous.NextStep: Docusign is out. Calling morning of 11/2 if it is not complete
previous.Business_Issue_Details__c: Ben planned to fully exit Red Rover IT by year end, but former customers and team members asked to come back, so he is relaunching as a new hybrid MSP built around a small, tight customer base. He wants the new company on one simple, low-overhead platform for PSA and billing instead of rebuilding on the patchwork of ConnectWise, Autotask, Odoo and a bare-bones SkySwitch billing instance he has cycled through over the years.
previous.Problems__c:
- Lost revenue: $300-$500/mo ($3.6K-$6K/yr) leaks from missed and uncharged services; onsite visits went unbilled.
- Billing accuracy: Hand-keyed billing and manual ACH with no auto-matching let a $200 error go unnoticed for 3 months.
- Admin time: Owner loses a full business day every month reconciling 30-50 invoices across 2 billing systems.
- Customer experience: ~20 customers get separate IT, telecom and one-time invoices, causing confusion and missed payments.
- Tool sprawl: 2 ERP instances (~$600/mo) with ticketing that loses asset history and leaves tickets open after resolution.
previous.Solutions__c:
- Agreements bundle every service and tie ticket time to billing, so recurring and onsite work is always invoiced.
- Automated recurring billing plus Rev.io Payments autopay with auto-reconciliation catch errors before they post.
- Scheduled batch billing runs with per-service intervals and multiple bill cycles replace the monthly billing day.
- One consolidated statement per customer, parent-child rollups for school districts and a self-service portal.
- PSA Web and billing on one platform with full asset service history, Revii summaries and mobile ticket close-out.
previous.Values__c: Rev.io recovers $3.6K-$6K/yr in leaked revenue and gives Ben back a full day every month by putting billing, payments and service on one platform. Consolidating tools saves another ~$600-$700/mo while every customer gets a single accurate invoice.
